sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到我们的节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world.
sentences.zh: 新听众、老听众，无论你身处世界的哪个角落。

sentences.en: It is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 很高兴大家能回来收听又一期节目，当然，我们要在这里剖析20多岁时的心理学。

sentences.en: So I don't know about you, but it often feels like my 20s, they aren't just about like growing and experiencing life.
sentences.zh: 我不知道你们是怎么想的，但我常常觉得，在20多岁的时候，生活不仅仅是关于成长和体验人生。

sentences.en: There's almost this implicit feeling that they're actually about ticking off a checkliSt.
sentences.zh: 这里几乎有一种潜移默化的感觉，觉得这个阶段其实就是为了在一个清单上打勾。

sentences.en: You know, some people call it like the 30 before 30, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，有些人管这叫“三十岁前要做的三十件事”，对吧？

sentences.en: Moving out of home, graduating university, tick, get a good job, tick, find a life partner, solidify, like your lifetime friendship group,
sentences.zh: 搬出去单住、大学毕业、打勾，找份好工作、打勾，找到人生伴侣、巩固你一辈子的朋友圈，

sentences.en: buy a house, travel, invest, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 买房、旅游、投资，等等等等。

sentences.en: There is this very almost omnipresent blueprint given to us by society, by our peers, by our parents, by the media about how this decade is meant to look.
sentences.zh: 社会、同龄人、父母以及媒体给我们提供了一份几乎无处不在的蓝图，告诉我们这十年该是什么样子。

sentences.en: And it's quite linear and consecutive.
sentences.zh: 而且它相当线性且一脉相承。

sentences.en: It's constantly moving forwards and upwards.
sentences.zh: 它总是在不断地向前、向上发展。

sentences.en: But what if you are one of those people, one of many of us, who find themselves completely starting over in their 20s, starting from scratch?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你是那种人呢——也就是我们当中许多发现自己在20多岁时彻底一切推倒重来、从零开始的人？

sentences.en: The carefully laid plans, you know, kind of may have crumbled to the future that we'd imagined and had been so sure of suddenly doesn't seem that fun and enjoyable anymore.
sentences.zh: 那些精心铺排的计划可能已经破灭，曾经想象过并笃信不疑的未来突然间好像也没那么有趣、那么令人期待了。

sentences.en: Maybe we've realized that we've made a mistake.
sentences.zh: 也许我们意识到自己犯了错。

sentences.en: We need to leave the relationship, leave the job, leave the city we're in, leave the friendship, leave the life that we've kind of created so far.
sentences.zh: 我们需要离开这段感情、离开这份工作、离开所在的城市、离开这段友谊、离开我们迄今为止建立起来的生活。

sentences.en: That is a reality for a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 这对于我们很多人来说都是现实。

sentences.en: It is very hard to admit to ourselves when and that we do need to start over.
sentences.zh: 要向自己承认何时以及我们确实需要重新开始，是一件非常困难的事。

sentences.en: So hard, in fact, I think that few of us ever really do.
sentences.zh: 事实上，正因为太难了，我觉得我们当中很少有人真正能做到。

sentences.en: Instead, we endure a life and we endure a reality that doesn't fit us because the prospect of the unknown and of starting over feels not only shameful, but very scary.
sentences.zh: 相反，我们咬牙忍受着一种并不适合我们的生活和现实，因为面对未知和重新开始的前景不仅让人感到羞耻，而且非常可怕。

sentences.en: However, when we do admit it to ourselves that we are ready to start over or when that decision is kind of thrust on us,
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们真正向自己承认我们已经准备好重新开始，或者当这种决定被强加在我们身上时，

sentences.en: I think it can be quite liberating if we take a different perspective on it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们换一个角度来看待它，我觉得这其实会相当具有解放意义。

sentences.en: Now, I don't want to discount that there is going to be fear there.
sentences.zh: 当然，我并不想否认其中会伴随着恐惧。

sentences.en: There is going to be confusion, especially since we feel like we've fallen off the blueprint.
sentences.zh: 也会有困惑，尤其是当我们觉得仿佛偏离了人生蓝图的时候。

sentences.en: We maybe don't have plans anymore.
sentences.zh: 我们可能不再有计划了。

sentences.en: We don't have seemingly in our mind an ideal sense of the future.
sentences.zh: 我们的脑海中似乎不再有一个对未来的理想愿景。

sentences.en: But I really want to talk about why that is okay and why this is actually a very common experience.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很想谈谈为什么这其实没关系，为什么这其实是一种非常普遍的经历。

sentences.en: And if you're feeling isolated, overwhelmed, maybe shameful as we, you know, ashamed, as we mentioned before, that is exactly what I would expect you to be feeling in this moment.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到孤立无援、不知所措，或者正如我们刚才提到的那样感到羞耻，这恰恰就是我在这种时刻所能预料到的你的感受。

sentences.en: But it shouldn't discourage you or shouldn't make you feel like you haven't made the right choice or that this is actually going to turn out completely, entirely okay.
sentences.zh: 但这不应该打击你的积极性，也不应该让你觉得你做了错误的选择，或者觉得这一切最终一定会走向一个完全、彻底圆满的结局。

sentences.en: We are going to discuss some of the common ways that we are forced to start over in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 我们接下来要讨论的是我们在20多岁时被迫重新开始的一些常见方式。

sentences.en: The biggest reasons why we have so much fear towards this experience, whether that's because of timeline comparison or the fear of the unknown,
sentences.zh: 我们对这种经历产生如此多恐惧的最大原因，无论是出于时间线的比较还是对未知的恐惧，

sentences.en: lots of identity, our attachment to comfort.
sentences.zh: 身份认同的迷失，以及我们对舒适圈的依恋。

sentences.en: We're going to discuss all of those factors.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论所有这些因素。

sentences.en: Plus, and this is the most important part of this episode, how to shift from that really fear-based mindset to an opportunity-based mindset
sentences.zh: 此外——这也是本期节目最核心的部分——当你面临在20多岁重新开始的机会时，

sentences.en: when you encounter the opportunity to start over in your 20s.
sentences.zh: 如何从那种基于恐惧的心态转变为基于机遇的心态。

sentences.en: I also really want to share some listener stories.
sentences.zh: 我还特别想分享一些听众的故事。

sentences.en: I've been doing that more and more because I just feel like there is so much wisdom from the community.
sentences.zh: 我越来越频繁地这样做，因为我觉得社区里蕴含着太多的智慧。

sentences.en: And sometimes I think just hearing that other people are going through what you are going through is the assurance that we all need.
sentences.zh: 有时我觉得，仅仅是听到别人也在经历着与你相同的境遇，就是我们所有人最需要的抚慰。

sentences.en: And I want to remind you, just because something about your life isn't working out right now, doesn't mean that the rest of your life is doomed.
sentences.zh: 我想提醒你，仅仅因为你目前的生活有些地方不如意，并不意味着你的余生就此毁了。

sentences.en: That is the main philosophy and theme that we will be promoting in this episode.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们将在本期节目中倡导的核心哲学和主题。

sentences.en: So I hope that if you are in this position, this brings you comfort, knowledge, information, maybe just a sense of calm.
sentences.zh: 所以，我希望如果你正处在这个位置上，这能为你带来安慰、知识、信息，或者仅仅是一种内心平静感。

sentences.en: And without further ado, let's get into the episode.
sentences.zh: 废话不多说，让我们进入今天的节目。

sentences.en: What does it feel like to start over in your 20s?
sentences.zh: 在20多岁时一切推倒重来是一种什么样的感觉？

sentences.en: I want to share a story from a listener, actually, to start us off.
sentences.zh: 其实，我想先分享一位听众的故事来开启今天的节目。

sentences.en: And I think this story just really captures the, I don't know, the essence of what it feels like to start over.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个故事完美地捕捉到了那种，怎么说呢，重新开始的真实本质。

sentences.en: Hey, Gemma, I want to share my story of starting over in hopes that it will help someone else feel less like a failure because they didn't get it right the first time.
sentences.zh: “嗨，詹玛，我想分享我重新开始的故事，希望它能帮助其他人少一点觉得自己是个失败者的挫败感，就因为他们没有在第一次尝试时就做对。”

sentences.en: When I was 27, I had my dream job.
sentences.zh: “当我27岁的时候，我拥有着我梦寐以求的工作。”

sentences.en: I was making commercials, working my way up to potentially being a film director.
sentences.zh: “我在拍广告，一步步往上爬，有望成为一名电影导演。”

sentences.en: I had all of these friends, a nice flat.
sentences.zh: “我有一群好朋友，还有一个不错的公寓。”

sentences.en: I was living in London with my boyfriend who I'd met at 22.
sentences.zh: “我住在伦敦，和我的男朋友在一起，我们是在我22岁时认识的。”

sentences.en: We lived together and we had a cat.
sentences.zh: “我们同居了，还养了一只猫。”

sentences.en: And I thought for sure he was going to propose in the next year.
sentences.zh: “我当时笃定他会在接下来的一年里向我求婚。”

sentences.en: Everything basically just seemed laid out perfectly in front of me.
sentences.zh: “一切看起来都完美地呈现在我的眼前。”

sentences.en: Within the span of two months, I lost my job when COVID started.
sentences.zh: “但在短短两个月内，新冠疫情爆发，我失业了。”

sentences.en: My boyfriend broke up with me because he caught feelings for one of his co-workers.
sentences.zh: “我男朋友跟我分手了，因为他对一个女同事动了心。”

sentences.en: And my dad had a stroke.
sentences.zh: “而且我爸爸中风了。”

sentences.en: So I moved back home to take care of him.
sentences.zh: “于是我搬回老家去照顾他。”

sentences.en: Enter my dark days.
sentences.zh: “我的至暗时刻就此登场。”

sentences.en: For the next year, it felt like my trajectory was permanently changed.
sentences.zh: “在接下来的一年里，我感觉自己的人生轨迹被永久地改写了。”

sentences.en: And I was going to be a failure and miserable.
sentences.zh: “我觉得自己注定要失败，而且会痛苦不堪。”

sentences.en: This was the beginning of the end.
sentences.zh: “这就是末日的开始。”

sentences.en: I hadn't felt this uncertain since I was 17.
sentences.zh: “自从我17岁以来，我就再没有感到过如此这般的不确定。”

sentences.en: Because in the last 10 years, the next step had always been obvious for me.
sentences.zh: “因为在过去这十年里，我的下一步总是显而易见的。”

sentences.en: And I guess I took that for granted.
sentences.zh: “而我当时大概把这当成了理所当然。”

sentences.en: Slowly but surely, I started to really think, what do I want the next 10 years of my life to look like?
sentences.zh: “慢慢地，但坚定不移地，我开始认真思考：我希望我人生的下一个十年是什么样子的？”

sentences.en: What is going to make me happy?
sentences.zh: “什么才能真正让我快乐？”

sentences.en: I started to put things into action.
sentences.zh: “我开始把想法付诸行动。”

sentences.en: And now I can confidently say that I am happier than ever.
sentences.zh: “而现在我可以自信地说，我比以往任何时候都要快乐。”

sentences.en: My dad got better.
sentences.zh: “我爸爸身体好转了。”

sentences.en: And now I live in Italy.
sentences.zh: “我现在住在意大利。”

sentences.en: And I teach yoga.
sentences.zh: “我还是一名瑜伽老师。”

sentences.en: I got certified two years ago.
sentences.zh: “我在两年前获得了认证。”

sentences.en: I run my own business as well.
sentences.zh: “我也在经营着自己的生意。”

sentences.en: I live in my own apartment with my two cats now.
sentences.zh: “我现在和我的两只猫一起住在属于我自己的公寓里。”

sentences.en: And I have a beautiful community around me.
sentences.zh: “我的身边有着一个美好的社区。”

sentences.en: It honestly scares me to think that this life almost didn't happen.
sentences.zh: “一想到这种生活差一点就错过了，我就真的感到后怕。”

sentences.en: And that I thought what I had before was the peak of happiness.
sentences.zh: “也庆幸我当时居然以为我以前拥有的就是幸福的巅峰。”

sentences.en: Not even close.
sentences.zh: “那简直差得十万八千里。”

sentences.en: So this email.
sentences.zh: “所以这封邮件……”

sentences.en: I got this email before I even announced that I was going to do this episode.
sentences.zh: “我在甚至还没宣布要录制这期节目之前，就收到了这封邮件。”

sentences.en: This person must have just known that maybe someone else out there needed to hear it.
sentences.zh: “这个人一定是有所感应，觉得外面的某个人可能正需要听到这些。”

sentences.en: And it honestly left me really emotional.
sentences.zh: “这真的让我感慨万千、情绪激昂。”

sentences.en: And I just want to repeat my favorite part once more because it's incredible.
sentences.zh: “我只想把最喜欢的那段话再重复一遍，因为它实在是太不可思议了。”

sentences.en: This is the part that I love.
sentences.zh: “这就是我爱不释手的那段。”

sentences.en: It honestly scares me to think that this life almost didn't happen.
sentences.zh: “一想到这种生活差一点就错过了，我就真的感到后怕。”

sentences.en: Now is that not the most beautiful and wise reminder from someone who has lived through and experienced this thing that we kind of fear everything falling apart.
sentences.zh: “这难道不是来自一个曾经亲历并体验过我们所有人都在恐惧的‘一切土崩瓦解’的人，最美丽、最睿智的提醒吗？”

sentences.en: That is what happened to her.
sentences.zh: “这就是她所经历的。”

sentences.en: And she's fine now.
sentences.zh: “而她现在过得很好。”

sentences.en: You know I just couldn't not include this story because sometimes like I said just hearing
sentences.zh: “你们知道我真的不能不把这个故事收录进来，因为正如我所说，有时候仅仅是听到”

sentences.en: how someone else's circumstances have turned out is enough to soothe our own doubt in a way.
sentences.zh: “别人的境遇最终迎来了好转，就足以在某种程度上抚平我们内心的自我怀疑。”

sentences.en: I think this story is also incredible because it touches on three very unique ways that we may be forced to start over in our 20s.
sentences.zh: “我认为这个故事之所以同样不可思议，是因为它触及了我们在20多岁时可能被迫重新开始的三种截然不同的方式。”

sentences.en: Relationships, career and location but also family and priorities.
sentences.zh: “人际关系、职业和地点，同时还有家庭和生活重心的排序。”

sentences.en: So actually almost five.
sentences.zh: “所以实际上差不多有五种。”

sentences.en: And each of them feels so uniquely significant.
sentences.zh: “而且每一种都显得如此具有独特的重大意义。”

sentences.en: It just blows my mind that this person experienced so many different you know so many different ways of life becoming chaotic all at once and she survived.
sentences.zh: “我简直不敢相信这个人竟然同时经历了这么多不同、那么多不同方面的生活在一瞬间陷入混乱，而她竟然熬过来了。”

sentences.en: So let's talk about the ways in which we might be forced to start over and I'm going to focus
sentences.zh: “所以，让我们来聊聊我们可能会被迫重新开始的那些方式，我打算先从”

sentences.en: on career first because I think when our career intentions and dreams change or our path becomes
sentences.zh: “职业开始，因为我觉得当我们的职业意图和梦想改变，或者我们的道路变得”

sentences.en: unclear we can feel very unmoored usually because our identity is somewhat if not seriously tied
sentences.zh: “模糊不清时，我们会感到非常没有方向感，这通常是因为我们的身份在某种程度上——甚至可以说是严重地——与”

sentences.en: to our vocation and what we do for a living what we're pursuing especially in our 20s right.
sentences.zh: “我们的职业以及我们谋生的手段、我们所追求的事物紧密相连，尤其是在我们20多岁的时候，对吧？”

sentences.en: It just feels like work is at the center.
sentences.zh: “我们总觉得工作是核心。”

sentences.en: We are meant to be climbing the corporate ladder working really hard figuring out what we want
sentences.zh: “我们本该在企业阶梯上不断往上爬，拼命工作，弄清楚自己想”

sentences.en: to do so when we don't feel like we know or we feel like we do know and it's not working out it can be very distressing.
sentences.zh: “做什么，所以当我们觉得一无所知，或者觉得自以为清楚却又行不通时，就会感到非常痛苦。”

sentences.en: There are many ways that this kind of happens to us.
sentences.zh: “这种事情发生在我们身上的方式有很多种。”

sentences.en: You may have been unexpectedly fired or made redundant in the last couple of years.
sentences.zh: “你可能在过去几年里意料之外地被解雇了，或者成为了裁员的对象。”

sentences.en: You may even get to a stage where you realize that you're just faking it you know this isn't what you want anymore or the industry is changing and you just can't get the job.
sentences.zh: “你甚至可能到了这样一个阶段：你意识到自己只是在装模作样，你知道的，这已经不是你想要的生活了，或者行业正在发生变化，而你根本找不到工作。”

sentences.en: You've pushed yourself so hard you're not getting any traction.
sentences.zh: “你把自己逼得太紧，却没有任何进展。”

sentences.en: Sometimes we reach a tipping point in these circumstances where we realize okay I gave it a go it might be time to abandon ship.
sentences.zh: “有时在这些情况下，我们会达到一个临界点，意识到：好吧，我已经尽力去尝试了，或许是时候跳船了。”

sentences.en: I'm not happy here anymore it's not working out and yes the future feels unclear but so does this current timeline that I'm on.
sentences.zh: “我在这里不再快乐了，这行不通了；是的，未来感觉一片模糊，但我目前身处的时间线同样也是一片模糊。”

sentences.en: When you really actually consider it and sit with this reality for a lot of people you kind
sentences.zh: “当你真正去思考、去直面这个现实时，对于很多人来说，你就会”

sentences.en: of realize that a lot of us are basically forced to put ourselves on a career or a professional trajectory very early on at like 17 or 18 years old.
sentences.zh: “意识到，我们中的许多人在大概17、18岁时，基本上就被迫走上了一条职业或专业发展的轨道。”

sentences.en: And I don't know about you but 17 year old Gemma she had no idea what she wanted.
sentences.zh: “我不知道你们怎么样，但17岁的詹玛她根本不知道自己想要什么。”

sentences.en: She thought she knew she thought she was a genius she thought she had it all figured out absolutely no way she was so naive.
sentences.zh: “她以为自己知道，她觉得自己是个天才，她觉得自己把一切都想明白了，绝对不可能，她当时太天真了。”

sentences.en: That was a big wake-up call when you know I started to think huh maybe what I dreamt about
sentences.zh: “那真是一个巨大的警钟，当我知道的——”

sentences.en: at 17 or 18 isn't what 24 year old me actually cares about anymore and if you're going through
sentences.zh: “当我开始思考：‘哈，也许我在17、18岁时梦想的东西，已经不再是24岁的我真正关心的了’，如果你现在正经历”

sentences.en: that right now I really feel for you but I also think it's important to actually periodically
sentences.zh: “这一切，我真的对你感同身受，但我同时也觉得，定期反思”

sentences.en: reflect on what you actually want from your professional life and make changes where you deem necessary kind of before it's too late.
sentences.zh: “你究竟想从职业生涯中得到什么，并在你认为必要的时候做出改变，这种做法非常重要，某种程度上要在为时已晚之前行动。”

sentences.en: The second biggest dimension area where we feel like we could be starting over is our relationships.
sentences.zh: “我们觉得可能需要重新开始的第二大维度领域，就是我们的人际关系。”

sentences.en: Now I mean both platonic and romantic but let's really zoom in on romantic for a second.
sentences.zh: “这里我指的是柏拉图式的友情和浪漫的爱情，但让我们先把镜头聚焦在浪漫爱情上。”

sentences.en: So I was talking to my friend Steph the other day about something that's happening in our friendship circle which is there has been a series of long-term relationship breakups that
sentences.zh: “前几天我跟我的朋友斯蒂芬聊起一件发生在我们朋友圈里的事情，那就是有一连串的长期恋爱关系”

sentences.en: have occurred amongst our friends and I am talking like 5, 7, 10 year relationships all coming to an end.
sentences.zh: “在我们的朋友中间宣告结束，我说的是那种维持了5年、7年、10年的恋爱关系全都走到了尽头。”

sentences.en: It's like everyone turns 27, realizes they're closer to 30 than ever before, their Saturn returns and they break up.
sentences.zh: “这就像每个人一到27岁，就会意识到自己离30岁比以往任何时候都要近，他们的土星回归到来，然后他们就分手了。”

sentences.en: So that period between around 27 to 29 is when a lot of us experience our first major breakup with a long-term partner.
sentences.zh: “所以27岁到29岁之间的那段时期，是我们很多人经历与长期伴侣的第一次重大分手的阶段。”

sentences.en: Maybe that's someone that you've fallen in love with in your early 20s and now you know you
sentences.zh: “也许那是你在20岁出头时坠入爱河的人，现在你知道”

sentences.en: are faced with the idea of entering 30 with them you realize that you want to enter it with someone
sentences.zh: “你面临着要和他们一起迈入30岁大关的想法，你意识到你想和”

sentences.en: else but it's very common for people to reach their late 20s and see a real flip in their relationship priorities and it's not a coincidence.
sentences.zh: “另一个人一起迈入这个阶段，但人们在快到30岁时发现自己的恋爱优先级发生彻底的转变，这并不是巧合。”

sentences.en: It's been suggested by some social psychologists that 27 to 30, 27 to 29 is a very serious and key
sentences.zh: 一些社会心理学家指出，27到30岁、27到29岁是恋爱关系中非常严肃且关键的

sentences.en: stage in relationships where you're kind of at this age where you either get serious or you get out.
sentences.zh: 一个阶段，你大概正处于这个年龄：要么关系变得认真，要么就此分道扬镳。

sentences.en: I think that's how a lot of us feel.
sentences.zh: 我想这也是我们许多人的切身感受。

sentences.en: This is also known by another name.
sentences.zh: 这个现象还有另一个名字。

sentences.en: It's called the 7 year itch.
sentences.zh: 它被称为七年之痒。

sentences.en: I don't know if you've heard that name before but it basically refers to this idea that at
sentences.zh: 我不知道你以前是否听说过这个词，但它基本上是指这样一种观点：

sentences.en: around 7 years a relationship either needs to change or needs to be left behind and either you evolve together or you go your separate ways.
sentences.zh: 大约在第七个年头，一段关系要么需要改变，要么需要被抛在身后，要么你们共同成长，要么各奔东西。

sentences.en: This is actually one of the main like timeline hurdles for a relationship.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是恋爱关系中主要的几道时间线坎坷之一。

sentences.en: It's typically 6 months, 2 years and 7 years.
sentences.zh: 通常是6个月、2年和7年。

sentences.en: Those are the times in which people are most likely to break up.
sentences.zh: 这些正是人们最容易分手的节点。

sentences.en: It follows a very similar pattern for a lot of us.
sentences.zh: 对我们许多人来说，它遵循着非常相似的模式。

sentences.en: Even as I'm telling you this though you might be comforted by the science.
sentences.zh: 不过，即使我这么跟你说，科学的研究或许也能给你带来一些安慰。

sentences.en: You might be able to say oh okay so this is normal.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，哦，原来这是正常的。

sentences.en: I don't think that reduces the fact that it's a very serious, deep, profoundly moving loss.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这并不能减轻这种失落感——那是一种非常严重、深沉且直击心灵的失落。

sentences.en: No one enters a relationship thinking this has an expiry date and at 27 I'll break up and find someone new.
sentences.zh: 没有人进入一段感情时会想：这玩意儿是有保质期的，我到27岁就会分手并找个新对象。

sentences.en: Typically we are in it for the long haul.
sentences.zh: 通常我们都是奔着长久去的。

sentences.en: We're committed to this person.
sentences.zh: 我们对这个人许下了承诺。

sentences.en: So I also think that even if you know deep down this is what is right, you will find someone else or you will be okay alone, it doesn't lessen the sting at least in the first 3 to
sentences.zh: 所以我也觉得，即使你内心深处知道这是对的，你会找到别人，或者自己一个人也能过得很好，但这并不能减轻那种刺痛，至少在头3到

sentences.en: 6 months.
sentences.zh: 6个月里是这样的。

sentences.en: It's definitely I think not made any easier by this societal stigma around being single and the sense that if you're not partnered up, you are not whole.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，社会对单身状态的污名化，以及“如果你没有伴侣，你就不完整”这种观念，绝对让这一切变得更加艰难。

sentences.en: You're either in a couple or you're half a person.
sentences.zh: 要么你是成双成对的，要么你只是半个人。

sentences.en: You must be either looking for love or in love.
sentences.zh: 你必然要么在寻找爱情，要么正沐浴爱河。

sentences.en: You know how could you possibly be in that middle space of just being happy by yourself?
sentences.zh: 你知道，怎么可能有人处在那种中间状态，仅仅是独自一人就觉得很开心呢？

sentences.en: Another way that we typically start over in our 20s is financially.
sentences.zh: 我们在20多岁时通常会经历的另一种重新开始，是在经济上。

sentences.en: Maybe you've made a big purchase.
sentences.zh: 也许你进行了一笔大额消费。

sentences.en: Maybe you've lost money.
sentences.zh: 也许你亏了钱。

sentences.en: Maybe you've gone all in on traveling.
sentences.zh: 也许你把所有的钱都投在了旅行上。

sentences.en: You've come back with nothing.
sentences.zh: 结果回来时两手空空。

sentences.en: I see this a lot.
sentences.zh: 这种情况我见得很多。

sentences.en: I actually don't think it's a bad thing.
sentences.zh: 其实我倒不觉得这是一件坏事。

sentences.en: I think that what is money if it's not something that unlocks a better life for you?
sentences.zh: 钱如果不是用来为你开启更好生活的工具，那它又算什么呢？

sentences.en: And for some people, money unlocks the security and comfort of a home or of long-term financial stability.
sentences.zh: 对某些人来说，钱能换来一个家的安全感和舒适感，或者长期的财务稳定。

sentences.en: For others, it unlocks things like travel and it unlocks things like giving yourself the
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，它能换来旅行之类的体验，能换来满足你

sentences.en: experiences you maybe always wanted as a child or giving yourself kind of that texture to life.
sentences.zh: 儿时一直渴望的体验，或者给你的生活增添那种质感。

sentences.en: So financially, I think, obviously, I'm not going to give you financial advice and you do what is best for you and what feels most aligned with your life priorities.
sentences.zh: 所以在经济方面，显然，我不会给你提供理财建议，你要做的是对自己最好、最符合你生活优先级的事情。

sentences.en: But I think starting over financially in our 20s is not always this big, dark, looming cloud that is promising you failure for the rest of your years, right?
sentences.zh: 但我认为，我们在20多岁时在经济上重新开始，并不总是那团阴暗逼近、预示着你余生都将一事无成的乌云，对吧？

sentences.en: I don't think that it's a mistake to spend your money, even if it means not having as much as people your own age or feeling like you don't have as much saved as, you know, Tom
sentences.zh: 我不认为把钱花掉是个错误，哪怕这意味着你没有同龄人存那么多钱，或者让你觉得自己不像你知道的

sentences.en: down the road or Beth up the street.
sentences.zh: 汤姆或贝丝那样存下了那么多积蓄。

sentences.en: Also, kind of on a similar note, not really, but moving.
sentences.zh: 另外，顺着类似的话题——其实也不太算，那就是搬家。

sentences.en: This is a time, our 20s are a time when a lot of us want to live in and see new places.
sentences.zh: 20多岁这段时期，我们中的许多人都想去看看新地方并在那里生活。

sentences.en: The amount of friends that I have who have moved to London in the last year, shocking, shocking.
sentences.zh: 我身边在过去一年里搬去伦敦的朋友数量，真是惊人，太惊人了。

sentences.en: I have this joke that like every Australian turns 25 and moves to London and every person in the UK turns 25 and moves to Australia.
sentences.zh: 我经常开玩笑说，好像每个澳大利亚人一满25岁就会搬去伦敦，而每个英国人一满25岁就会搬去澳大利亚。

sentences.en: Like it honestly feels that way.
sentences.zh: 真的感觉就是这样。

sentences.en: But really, it is a time when we're looking for a refresh.
sentences.zh: 但说真的，这确实是我们渴望换个新环境的时期。

sentences.en: We're looking for a new environment.
sentences.zh: 我们在寻找全新的环境。

sentences.en: We're looking for new friends.
sentences.zh: 我们在寻找新的朋友。

sentences.en: Adjusting to that, though, isn't always going to be a fairy tale.
sentences.zh: 不过，要适应这一切并不总是一帆风顺的。

sentences.en: We like comfort.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢舒适区。

sentences.en: We like what we know.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢熟悉的事物。

sentences.en: And there will be probably a period of disconnect where you don't have the same community or knowledge of a city or a space that you did when you lived back at home.
sentences.zh: 而且可能会有一段脱节期，在这个时期里，你不再拥有像住在家里时那样熟悉的社区，也不再对某个城市或空间那么了解。

sentences.en: I have a rule for situations like this, though.
sentences.zh: 不过，对于这种情况我有一个原则。

sentences.en: If you are lucky enough to move to a new city or a new country, I need you to give it at least
sentences.zh: 如果你足够幸运能够搬到一个新的城市或国家，我需要你至少给它

sentences.en: six months, six months where you cannot decide whether to stay or to go, because that period of time is typically how long it does take to learn a new place, to solidify some new
sentences.zh: 六个月的时间，在这六个月里你不能决定是去是留，因为通常需要这么长的时间去了解一个新地方、建立一些新的

sentences.en: friendships, to feel comfortable in a new job and to get a sense of home.
sentences.zh: 友谊、在新的工作中找到舒适感，并培养出一种家的感觉。

sentences.en: So if part of your fresh start in your 20s has been a significant move and you're struggling, you're thinking, oh, my God, like, fuck, I made a terrible decision.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在20多岁的全新起点中包含了一次重大的搬迁，而且你正苦苦挣扎，心里想着：“天哪，靠，我做了个糟糕的决定。”

sentences.en: Please keep the six month rule in mind.
sentences.zh: 请把六个月原则记在心里。

sentences.en: One final way that we typically see people restarting during this decade is almost like a complete overhaul.
sentences.zh: 在这个十年里，我们看到人们重新开始的最后一种方式，几乎是一次彻底的大改造。

sentences.en: It's not to do with finances, it's not to do with relationships, career, it's everything.
sentences.zh: 这无关财务，无关感情，也无关职业，而是方方面面。

sentences.en: It is a refresh and a rebirth almost of our entire personality where we decide we need new hobbies, we need new beliefs, we need new clothes, new habits.
sentences.zh: 这几乎是对我们整个性格的一次刷新和重生，我们决定需要新的爱好、新的信仰、新的衣服、新的习惯。

sentences.en: It's part of our personal evolution.
sentences.zh: 这是我们个人演变的一部分。

sentences.en: And I think normally when we get to that point where we do feel like we need to transform ourselves
sentences.zh: 我想，通常当我们走到那个地步，真的觉得自己需要作为一个人进行蜕变时，

sentences.en: as people, we've definitely reached an internal or emotional tipping point where at some stage
sentences.zh: 我们肯定已经达到了某种内部或情感上的临界点：在某个阶段你意识到自己不再快乐，

sentences.en: you realize that you are no longer happy and you will never be happy in this current version of yourself.
sentences.zh: 而且在目前这个版本的自己身上，你将永远不会快乐。

sentences.en: So that is definitely another way that we are promised a fresh start in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 所以这绝对是我们在20多岁时注定会经历的另一种全新开始。

sentences.en: So these are the most common core examples.
sentences.zh: 以上就是最常见的一些核心例子。

sentences.en: I'll also say that at the time of recording this, you know, there are huge fires in LA and many people have had to start over because of something completely drastic, dramatic, out
sentences.zh: 我还要说的是，在我录制这段音频的时候，洛杉矶发生了特大火灾，许多人因为一些完全剧烈、戏剧性、

sentences.en: of their control, like a natural disaster.
sentences.zh: 超出他们控制的事情（比如自然灾害）而不得不重新开始。

sentences.en: And those experiences for other people sometimes really put into perspective our own probleMs.
sentences.zh: 有时，别人的这些经历确实能让我们自己的问题显得不那么严重。

sentences.en: But it really does go to show that you can do everything right and there can still be factors outside of your control that can get to you and that can force a fresh start.
sentences.zh: 但这也确实表明，即使你把一切都做对了，仍然可能会有你控制之外的因素影响到你，并迫使你重新开始。

sentences.en: So when we are either involuntarily or voluntarily pushed to restart and start over in our 20s, we
sentences.zh: 因此，当我们无论是非自愿还是自愿地被推着在20多岁时重新开始时，

sentences.en: are likely to encounter some pretty emotional, psychological, hard barriers or things that make it difficult and that bring about doubt and confusion.
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会遇到一些相当感性的、心理上的、困难的壁垒，或者那些带来阻碍、引发怀疑和困惑的事物。

sentences.en: And I want to talk about all of those after this short break.
sentences.zh: 在短暂的休息之后，我想谈谈所有这些内容。

sentences.en: Admitting to yourself and I guess to others that you have had to start over in your 20s in some capacity, it can bring about a lot of shame and fear.
sentences.zh: 向自己——我想也包括向别人——承认你在20多岁时不得不在某种程度上重新开始，这会带来很多的羞耻感和恐惧。

sentences.en: And we associate it with feeling like we failed or feeling like we're disappointing people or like you've wasted those early years.
sentences.zh: 我们会把这同失败感联系起来，觉得自己在让人失望，或者觉得自己浪费了那些早期的岁月。

sentences.en: Why does it feel so weird to admit to ourselves and to others that we're starting over?
sentences.zh: 为什么向自己和他人承认我们正在重新开始会感觉如此诡异？

sentences.en: I think the first reason that this is so hard, and I would say the primary reason in this generation, is timeline comparison.
sentences.zh: 我认为这之所以如此艰难的第一个原因，也可以说是这一代人中最主要的原因，就是时间线比较。

sentences.en: As humans, part of our DNA, I guess, part of our blueprint, our social blueprint,
sentences.zh: 作为人类，我们DNA的一部分，我想也是我们的蓝图、社会蓝图的一部分，

sentences.en: has evolved to compare, to look at our peers or our friends as a way to see whether we are doing this whole life thing correctly.
sentences.zh: 已经进化出了比较的本能，通过观察同龄人或朋友，来检验我们把整个人生这场大戏过得是否正确。

sentences.en: And if the majority of people are where we are, we largely assume we're doing okay.
sentences.zh: 如果大多数人的处境和我们一样，我们就会大体上觉得自己过得还行。

sentences.en: If they're at a similar point in, you know, their life as us, we kind of think, okay, no probleMs.
sentences.zh: 如果他们和我们处于人生中相似的阶段，我们就会想，好吧，没问题。

sentences.en: We're fine.
sentences.zh: 我们挺好的。

sentences.en: We're not going to fall behind.
sentences.zh: 我们不会落后。

sentences.en: No disaster.
sentences.zh: 没有灾难发生。

sentences.en: But if our perception of other people's progress and success is that they are much more advanced than us,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们对别人进展和成功的感知是他们比我们先进得多，

sentences.en: and that is the norm, we are engaging in something called upward social comparison.
sentences.zh: 并且这成为了常态，我们就会陷入一种叫做“向上社会比较”的机制中。

sentences.en: And that can really bring about a sense of pressure or shame, doubt, confusion that we are falling behind.
sentences.zh: 这确实会带来一种压力、羞耻感、怀疑和困惑，让我们觉得自己正在落后。

sentences.en: Milestone or life trajectory is probably one of the main things that we compare ourselves on in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 里程碑或人生轨迹可能是我们在20多岁时最常用来进行比较的事物之一。

sentences.en: Most likely because there is no guidebook for how well we should be going.
sentences.zh: 这很可能是因为对于我们应该把生活过得多好，并没有一本指南。

sentences.en: There is no unique, special way that we should be doing things.
sentences.zh: 并没有什么独特、特殊的方式规定我们该如何做事。

sentences.en: So we tend to use examples in our environment, like our friends, our similarly aged colleagues, people we see online, as a way to tell us.
sentences.zh: 所以我们往往会用环境中的例子，比如我们的朋友、年龄相仿的同事、我们在网上看到的人，来作为评判自己的标准。

sentences.en: We don't realize, though, when we do that, either consciously or unconsciously, we don't realize that we have a real blind spot.
sentences.zh: 然而，当我们这样做时，无论是清醒还是潜意识里，我们都没有意识到自己有一个真正的盲区。

sentences.en: We do not have an accurate sample.
sentences.zh: 我们没有一个准确的样本。

sentences.en: We are not seeing the whole picture.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到全貌。

sentences.en: We are not seeing the areas of these people's lives where they themselves feel behind.
sentences.zh: 我们没有看到这些人生活中他们自己也觉得落后的那些领域。

sentences.en: In fact, recent research would tell you that when we compare, we are actually most likely to choose the most accomplished person we know
sentences.zh: 事实上，最近的研究表明，当我们进行比较时，我们实际上最有可能选择我们认识的最有成就的人，

sentences.en: and treat them as the average when really they're not.
sentences.zh: 并把他们视为平均水平，而他们实际上并不是。

sentences.en: It's a cognitive bias that we have.
sentences.zh: 这是我们身上的一种认知偏差。

sentences.en: The truth is there is no one correct path, but we also tend to forget that because social comparison is not rational, it's emotional, it is going to make you feel more insecure
sentences.zh: 事实是，根本没有一条唯一的正确道路，但我们也往往会忘记这一点，因为社会比较不是理性的，而是感性的，它会让你感到更加不安，

sentences.en: as a way to motivate you in this very human way to be like everyone else.
sentences.zh: 以此作为一种非常人性的方式来激励你变得和大家一样。

sentences.en: Compounding this, I think, is this cultural narrative that we all encounter that our 20s are a make-or-break time,
sentences.zh: 雪上加霜的是，我认为我们都会遇到这样一种文化叙事：我们的20多岁是一个成败在此一举的时期，

sentences.en: one where we are supposed to have it all figured out or at least be on our way.
sentences.zh: 在这个时期里，我们应该把一切都弄清楚，或者至少已经在路上了。

sentences.en: And this pressure really feeds into imposter syndrome, making us feel like we are constantly falling short, that we don't deserve to be where we are,
sentences.zh: 这种压力确实滋生了冒名顶替综合征，让我们觉得自己的表现总是不达标，觉得自己不配拥有现在的成就，

sentences.en: or that even when we are somewhere that we're happy to be, we could be further along.
sentences.zh: 或者甚至当我们身处一个让我们感到快乐的地方时，也觉得本可以走得更远。

sentences.en: The thing is, is that this kind of timeline comparison, and I'm certainly not blaming you for indulging in it, I definitely do it as well.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这种时间线比较——我当然不是在责怪你沉溺于此，我自己也经常这么做。

sentences.en: Sometimes it's just instinctual, but it's actually not making it any easier for us to change our lives or to move in the direction that we want.
sentences.zh: 有时这只是本能，但这实际上并没有让我们更容易去改变生活或朝着我们想要的方向前进。

sentences.en: So there was a 2022 study from the University of Florida that found that the more frequently we compare ourselves on things like timelines,
sentences.zh: 佛罗里达大学在2022年进行过一项研究，发现我们在时间线等事情上越频繁地进行自我比较，

sentences.en: the fewer positive feelings we have about ourselves and the less we feel that we can act to change our life or be better, do better.
sentences.zh: 我们对自己产生的积极情绪就越少，我们就越觉得无力采取行动去改变生活、变得更好或做得更好。

sentences.en: So it becomes a bit of a trap.
sentences.zh: 所以这变成了一个有点类似陷阱的东西。

sentences.en: You feel shit in comparison to someone else that's going to make you feel like you have no capability or agency to make your life better.
sentences.zh: 同别人相比，你会觉得自己很糟糕，这会让你觉得自己没有能力或自主权去让生活变得更好。

sentences.en: So you stay stuck.
sentences.zh: 于是你陷入了停滞。

sentences.en: I think, again, what exacerbates this and makes it harder is when nobody is talking about it.
sentences.zh: 我想，再次加剧这种状况并让它变得更艰难的是，没有人公开谈论这件事。

sentences.en: And when nobody is willing to say, yeah, I made a mistake and I'm starting over, or this didn't work out and I'm starting over.
sentences.zh: 没有人愿意说：“是的，我犯了错，我要重新开始”或者“这行不通，我要重新开始”。

sentences.en: So just simply telling your story and being open about how your life is turning out and how it might not be turning out as planned,
sentences.zh: 因此，仅仅是因为不愿讲述自己的故事，不愿坦诚生活的发展轨迹可能并不如计划中那样顺利，

sentences.en: we feel like we are the only one who is experiencing this and we feel like we are admitting to some failure.
sentences.zh: 我们就会觉得自己是唯一一个经历这一切的人，并且觉得自己是在承认某种失败。

sentences.en: That brings a lot of shame about not just what we are doing, but our inherent qualities, right?
sentences.zh: 这不仅给我们正在做的事情带来了沉重的羞耻感，还牵扯到了我们内在的品质，对吧？

sentences.en: This is why it can be so painful because we think that admitting to our life plan not working out shows that we are someone who wasn't good enough, wasn't capable enough,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它会如此痛苦，因为我们认为承认自己的人生规划行不通，是在表明自己是一个不够优秀、能力不足、

sentences.en: wasn't resilient enough, didn't deserve some success, when really that is not the case.
sentences.zh: 不够韧性、不配获得某种成功的人，而事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Your brain logic in this instance is not working in your favor.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，你的大脑逻辑并没有站在你这一边。

sentences.en: It's actually sabotaging our ego and sense of self further, almost because it would prefer that we be the ones to tell ourselves that we're a failure
sentences.zh: 它实际上在进一步破坏我们的自我和自我感，几乎是因为它宁愿由我们自己来告诉自己是个失败者，

sentences.en: than have someone else tell us.
sentences.zh: 也不愿让别人来告诉我们。

sentences.en: So if we go into this and we have no examples of anyone else experiencing what we're experiencing or normalizing it and then we feel like we have to tell people and admit to it,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们经历这一切时，身边没有任何人经历过我们正在经历的事情，也没有人将其归于正常化，然后我们又觉得自己必须把真相告诉别人并承认这一切，

sentences.en: our brain's going to convince us that we are much more horrible, terrible, much more of a failure than we actually are, almost as a way to protect our ego
sentences.zh: 我们的大脑就会说服我们，让我们觉得自己比实际上更加糟糕、可怕、彻底是个失败者——这几乎成了一种保护我们自我意识的方式，

sentences.en: by injuring it in the first place.
sentences.zh: 通过在第一时间伤害它来达到保护的目的。

sentences.en: So comparison, a fear of failure, that's definitely what makes starting over externally scary, but let's talk about some of the internal, more personal reasons
sentences.zh: 所以比较、对失败的恐惧，绝对是让向外重新开始显得可怕的原因，但让我们来谈谈一些内在的、更个人的原因，

sentences.en: that we do tend to struggle in these situations.
sentences.zh: 正是这些原因让我们在这些情况下往往会苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: The first big one is a fear of the unknown.
sentences.zh: 第一个大原因就是对未知的恐惧。

sentences.en: Truly, any fear that you have comes down to this greater fear of the unknown because if you knew what was going to happen, if you knew that the snake wouldn't bite you,
sentences.zh: 真的，你所感到的任何恐惧归根结底都是对这种更大的未知的恐惧，因为如果你知道会发生什么，如果你知道蛇不会咬你，

sentences.en: the plane wouldn't crash, that everything would turn out okay, you wouldn't be scared.
sentences.zh: 飞机不会坠毁，一切都会安然无恙，你就不会害怕了。

sentences.en: You wouldn't be scared.
sentences.zh: 你就不会害怕了。

sentences.en: So it's the uncertainty that matters.
sentences.zh: 所以，真正起作用的是不确定性。

sentences.en: How many of us have wished someone would just be able to concretely say that for certain everything will be all right?
sentences.zh: 我们有多少人曾希望有人能够斩钉截铁地说一句，一切肯定都会好起来的？

sentences.en: Oh, and you know, by the way, in three months, that's when you're going to find the new job and you're going to meet your soulmate in approximately 17 months and nine days
sentences.zh: “哦，你知道吗，顺便说一句，三个月后，你就会找到新工作；大约在17个月零9天后，你就会遇到你的灵魂伴侣；

sentences.en: and in two weeks, you'll have one of those days where everything about this new life makes sense.
sentences.zh: 而在两周后，你将迎来这样一天：关于这个新生活的一切都会变得顺理成章。”

sentences.en: We all hunger and crave that kind of validation that we are on the right path.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人都极度渴望并渴求那种确认，即我们正走在正确的道路上。

sentences.en: Thing is, no one can tell us that.
sentences.zh: 问题是，没有人能这样告诉我们。

sentences.en: No one is going to be able to give you the answer and tell you when it's all going to fall into place.
sentences.zh: 没有人能给你答案，并告诉你这一切将在什么时候尘埃落定。

sentences.en: Therefore, we have to manage this very natural anxiety around the unknown by ourselves the best we can.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们只能尽最大努力去应对这种围绕未知的、非常自然的焦虑。

sentences.en: The alternative is staying attached to what is comfortable, the stagnant career, the unhappy relationship, the unfulfilling friendships, the city,
sentences.zh: 与之相对的选择是继续依恋那些舒适的事物：停滞不前的职业、不快乐的关系、毫无成长的友谊、那个城市、

sentences.en: the place that doesn't give you any joy.
sentences.zh: 那个无法给你带来任何快乐的地方。

sentences.en: You could always stay there.
sentences.zh: 你大可一直呆在那里。

sentences.en: You could always remain in this nice, comfortable, safe bubble because you are too scared of what might happen.
sentences.zh: 你大可一直留在这个美好、舒适、安全的泡沫里，因为你太害怕可能会发生的事情了。

sentences.en: I just don't think that is a good alternative.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得这不是一个好的替代选择。

sentences.en: And what are you going to be more glad that you did in a year, in five years, in 10 years?
sentences.zh: 一年后、五年后、十年后，什么会让你更加庆幸自己做过？

sentences.en: Are you going to be glad that you stayed safe and you stayed locked away?
sentences.zh: 你会庆幸自己保持安全、把自己锁在舒适区里吗？

sentences.en: Or are you going to be glad that you looked at your life, you said, I'm not happy here and you changed things?
sentences.zh: 还是会庆幸自己审视了生活，说出“我在这里并不快乐”，并作出了改变？

sentences.en: I do also want to offer you a different way of framing this, which is that life would be utterly and completely boring if you knew how it was all going to turn out.
sentences.zh: 我还想为你提供另一种看待这个问题的框架，那就是：如果你知道事情会如何收场，生活将会变得彻底而完全的无聊。

sentences.en: It would honestly be such a drag to know how everything was going to unfold down to the minute details, how everything was going to turn out.
sentences.zh: 老实说，如果连细枝末节都知道得一清二楚，知道一切将如何展开、事情最终会走向何方，那将是一件非常乏味的事。

sentences.en: Honestly, it would seem very pointless to be living this life with no anticipation and no surprises.
sentences.zh: 说实话，过这样一种没有期待、没有惊喜的人生，会显得毫无意义。

sentences.en: So even if there is not a lot of joy in not knowing and not a lot of joy in the chaos, I do think that the alternative would be even more horrendous.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使“不知道”本身并没有多少快乐，混乱中也没有多少快乐，但我确实认为，另一种选择会更加糟糕。

sentences.en: So let's talk about the final reason why I think starting over in our 20s is so hard.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们来谈谈我认为在20多岁时重新开始之所以如此艰难的最后一个原因。

sentences.en: And that is because of the loss of identity that we experience when we transition away from our career choices or our relationship or the places of comfort.
sentences.zh: 这是因为当我们告别职业选择、人际关系或舒适区时，会经历一种认同感的丧失。

sentences.en: A lot of people think that identity formation takes place in our childhood.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为身份认同的形成发生在我们的童年时期。

sentences.en: And in many ways, that is true.
sentences.zh: 在许多方面，确实如此。

sentences.en: But it also really gets tested and solidified in our 20s.
sentences.zh: 但它在我们的二十多岁时，同样会经受真正的考验并最终成型。

sentences.en: Our identity, I like to think about it as being made up of many buckets from values to culture to relationships, career, hobbies, appearance, beliefs.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把我们的身份认同想象成由许多部分组成，从价值观、文化到人际关系、职业、爱好、外表和信仰。

sentences.en: We tend to piece our identity together from things that surround us and attach significance to positions and roles like our job title, like who we're dating,
sentences.zh: 我们往往从周围的事物中拼凑出自我认同，并将意义赋予各种职位和角色，比如我们的职位头衔、我们在和谁约会，

sentences.en: like where we live, our environment.
sentences.zh: 比如我们住在哪里、我们的环境。

sentences.en: Now, when those things naturally fall away, when we are forced to start over, when some spanner is thrown into the wheel, we feel very unmoored from the pillars of who we are.
sentences.zh: 然而，当这些东西自然而然地离去，当我们被迫重新开始，当生活中出现意料之外的波折时，我们会觉得自己就像失去了锚点的船，找不到自我的核心支柱。

sentences.en: You're kind of just left with a few remnants of your identity when material or I guess outside things fall away.
sentences.zh: 当物质或外界的东西流逝时，你身边其实只剩下少数几样关于你身份的残余。

sentences.en: So let me use the example of a long-term relationship.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我以一段长期恋爱关系为例。

sentences.en: When a long-term relationship ends, often people will struggle rebuilding a full and complete sense of self because they've really tied themselves up in this other person.
sentences.zh: 当一段长期恋情结束时，人们往往很难重建完整而全面的自我意识，因为他们把太多的自我都系在了另一个人身上。

sentences.en: So they may have neglected the things that really do make them unique, like their interests or their beliefs or their values.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可能忽视了那些真正让他们变得独特的东西，比如他们的兴趣、信仰或价值观。

sentences.en: And so you really have to work your way back to that place of deep self-knowledge because you can no longer rely on this relationship or this other person to define you.
sentences.zh: 因此，你必须重新找回那种深刻的自我认知，因为你不能再依靠这段关系或另一个人来定义你。

sentences.en: And that is going to be emotionally painful and stressful and scary if you didn't think you were going to be here.
sentences.zh: 如果你原本没料到会走到这一步，这将会带来情感上的痛苦、压力和恐惧。

sentences.en: I've seen this happen in so many friends' relationships.
sentences.zh: 我曾在许多朋友的恋爱中见过这种情况。

sentences.en: And to be completely honest with you,
sentences.zh: 老实跟你说，

sentences.en: I'm sure that if me and my boyfriend or my partner broke up right now, it would be likely that I would fall into this same spiral.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，如果我和我男友或伴侣现在分手了，我也很有可能会陷入同样的漩涡。

sentences.en: Because naturally, when you care about someone, when you're imagining your future with them,
sentences.zh: 因为很自然地，当你关心一个人，当你幻想着和他们共同的未来时，

sentences.en: that would allow you to be fully independent and that would allow your identity to be fully formed on your own.
sentences.zh: 这能让你保持完全的独立，并让你的身份完全由你自己塑造。

sentences.en: I don't think that's a bad thing at all.
sentences.zh: 我一点也不觉得这有什么不好。

sentences.en: I think that's a sign of healthy reliance and dependency.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是健康依赖和依恋的标志。

sentences.en: It is just an adjustment.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个适应过程。

sentences.en: Okay, so far we have really zoned in on explaining the hard parts of starting over and why our feelings about it do emerge.
sentences.zh: 好了，到目前为止，我们已经深入探讨了重新开始的艰难之处，以及为什么我们会产生这些感受。

sentences.en: I think it is time that we shift to a more future-oriented, positive approach and really examine how we can use psychology and what we know about ourselves as humans to use these
sentences.zh: 我想是时候转向一种更具前瞻性、更积极的方法了，让我们真正审视如何运用心理学以及我们对人类自身的了解，将这些

sentences.en: unfortunate fresh starts to our advantage.
sentences.zh: 不幸的重新开始转化为我们的优势。

sentences.en: So when we come back,
sentences.zh: 所以等我们回来后，

sentences.en: I'm going to talk advice,
sentences.zh: 我会分享一些建议，

sentences.en: I'm going to talk leveraging transitional periods and why the best time to start over is actually right now.
sentences.zh: 我将谈谈如何利用转型期，以及为什么重新开始的最佳时机其实就是现在。

sentences.en: We'll be back right after this short break.
sentences.zh: 这段简短的广告后马上回来。

sentences.en: So I want to tell you why the best time for you to start over is right now as promised.
sentences.zh: 正如承诺的那样，我想告诉大家为什么现在就是你重新开始的最佳时机。

sentences.en: If you were going to choose a moment to reinvent yourself and to leave environments, people and places that don't serve you in your 20s, it would be right now.
sentences.zh: 如果你要在二十多岁时选择一个时刻来重塑自我，并离开那些不再适合你的环境、人和地方，那就是现在。

sentences.en: You will never be as young with as much future time in front of you as you have in this moment.
sentences.zh: 你再也不会像此刻这样年轻，眼前有着如此广阔的未来。

sentences.en: You can spend hours, weeks, months ruminating on what could have happened.
sentences.zh: 你可以花上几个小时、几周甚至几个月，反复琢磨原本可能会发生什么。

sentences.en: You can reflect and think, if I'd just done this, if I'd just done that.
sentences.zh: 你可以反思并想着：如果我当时做了这个，如果我当时做了那个就好了。

sentences.en: But these hypotheticals are not in the realm of your control.
sentences.zh: 但这些假设并不在你的控制范围之内。

sentences.en: So unfortunate as it is, I think it is a lost cause to reflect on the past with longing because it can't change anything.
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管很遗憾，我认为带着留恋去回顾过去是无济于事的，因为它改变不了任何事情。

sentences.en: But luckily, you have been given the gift of a new beginning.
sentences.zh: 但幸运的是，你得到了一个新开始的馈赠。

sentences.en: And your 20s are a great time to start over again and again and again because of just how flexible and adaptable we are and our lives are and our brains are.
sentences.zh: 二十多岁是不断重新开始的绝佳时期，因为我们、我们的生活以及我们的大脑都具有极强的灵活性和适应能力。

sentences.en: It is such a unique time for reinvention.
sentences.zh: 这是一个重塑自我的绝佳时期。

sentences.en: Although, you know, our brains continue to change and develop over our lifetime, our 20s are actually the second most formative period for brain development in our life.
sentences.zh: 尽管你知道，我们的大脑在整个一生中都在不断变化和发展，但二十多岁实际上是我们一生中大脑发育的第二大关键时期。

sentences.en: And that works in your favor.
sentences.zh: 这对你非常有利。

sentences.en: It's easier for you to rewire certain pathways, to form new attachments, to learn new skills, to be resilient because we are so adaptable and you can create a whole new
sentences.zh: 你更容易重塑某些神经回路、形成新的依恋、学习新技能并培养韧性，因为我们极具适应力，你可以围绕着正在创造的这个全新生活，构建一个全新的

sentences.en: neurological system based on this new life you're creating.
sentences.zh: 神经系统。

sentences.en: I think we all know the saying, you can't teach an old dog new tricks.
sentences.zh: 我想大家都听过这句俗语：江山易改，本性难移。

sentences.en: And in some ways that's true.
sentences.zh: 在某些方面确实如此。

sentences.en: The older you get, the harder it is to give yourself the gift of a fresh start.
sentences.zh: 你越老，就越难给自己一个重新开始的机会。

sentences.en: I also want to remind you, you are still incredibly young.
sentences.zh: 我还想提醒你，你仍然非常年轻。

sentences.en: Even if you are listening to this and you're not in your 20s, you're in your early 30s or your early 40s, my gosh, there are people in their 60s,
sentences.zh: 即使你在听这个节目时已经不再是二十多岁，而是在三十岁出头或四十岁出头，天哪，还有那些六十岁、
七十岁、

sentences.en: 80s who would look at your life and say, to have the time you have, if only I had changed at your age, if only I had let myself.
sentences.zh: 八十岁的人，他们看着你的生活会说：要是我有你这样的时间就好了，要是我能在你这个年纪改变就好了，要是我当时允许自己改变就好了。

sentences.en: I think I've said this quote before actually, but it's one that really sticks with me.
sentences.zh: 我想我以前其实说过这句话，但它真的深深触动了我。

sentences.en: Also there's less consequences, you know, you don't have kids yet, you may not have a mortgage, you don't have other huge things to take care of that become more pressing
sentences.zh: 而且后果也更少，你知道的，你还没有孩子，你可能还没有房贷，你没有其他需要照顾的重大事情，随着年龄的增长，这些事情会变得更加紧迫

sentences.en: the older you get, you have more time in front of you than you have behind you.
sentences.zh: 你面前的时间比你身后的时间还要多。

sentences.en: So I really want you to remember that when you are stressed or anxious
sentences.zh: 所以我真的希望当你感到压力或焦虑时能记住这一点

sentences.en: about feeling like you failed the first time or you didn't get it right because that again is part of the interesting story you are writing and I think that is much
sentences.zh: 因为觉得第一次失败了或者没有做好而感到焦虑，因为那再次成为了你正在书写的精彩故事的一部分，我认为这比

sentences.en: more important than being able to say yeah I got it all right and did everything perfectly the first time and I never made mistakes.
sentences.zh: 能够说“太好了，我第一次就全做对了，每件事都做得完美无缺，而且我从来没犯过错”要重要得多。

sentences.en: Also means you never learned anything.
sentences.zh: 这也意味着你从来没有学到过任何东西。

sentences.en: So I hope this episode has provided you with some clarity, maybe just some peace, just a sense of like okay it's all going to be okay.
sentences.zh: 所以我希望这期节目能给你带来一些清晰的思路，也许只是一些平静，一种“没关系，一切都会好起来的”的感觉。

sentences.en: That is really all I hope for with any of these podcast episodes is just that you can you know hear the words and the voice of someone else in their 20s and go
sentences.zh: 这真的是我对任何一期播客的唯一期望，就是你能听到另一个20多岁的人的话语和声音，然后觉得

sentences.en: okay it's not just me because it definitely isn't.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不只是我一个人这样，因为绝对不只我一个。

sentences.en: Make sure that if you enjoyed this episode you share it with a friend, you share it on your Instagram story, anywhere and if you do actually tag me I love seeing the
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这期节目，请确保把它分享给朋友，分享到你的Instagram快拍上，或者任何地方，如果你确实艾特了我，我喜欢看到

sentences.en: different parts of the world where people are listening.
sentences.zh: 世界各地人们在收听节目的不同地方。

sentences.en: It's honestly one of my favorite parts of the day is being like oh my gosh someone in Kenya, someone in Brussels, someone in Bristol.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是我一天中最喜欢的部分之一，就像是“天哪，肯尼亚有人，布鲁塞尔有人，布里斯托尔也有人”。

sentences.en: So please feel free to share it over there.
sentences.zh: 所以请尽管去那里分享吧。

sentences.zh: 播客或Spotify上关注了我们，如果你喜欢这期节目，还留下了五星好评。

sentences.en: Also drop a comment below if you have further thoughts about reinvention and starting over in your 20s.
sentences.zh: 如果你对20多岁时的自我重塑和重新开始有更多的想法，也请在下方留言。

sentences.en: I love to keep the conversation going there and I just love to hear from you guys.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢在那里继续对话，我也非常喜欢听到你们的声音。
